summary: I used the final stretch on the one remaining open question and settled the half of it that source can settle, which turned out to matter for the report. The delivery of committed entries is a blocking select-send that nothing in the entry path times out or rejects, so a stalled main loop lasts exactly as long as the application's FSM lags — but the same select has a second arm on the shutdown channel, and Shutdown closes that channel, so a caller that already holds the Raft instance can release the stall by shutting the node down. That is precisely the escape the startup-replay finding lacks: there the identical send blocks before NewRaft has returned, so no caller can hold a handle to close that channel and the only reader is a goroutine the same constructor starts after the blocking call. Recording the distinction makes the two cases different in kind rather than in degree, and it is drawn from the two anchors rather than from a run, which is why I filed it as a source-only part-answer with the claim left unresolved: the behavioural half — whether such a stall is long enough to matter in that it stops RPC processing and the leader's own lease check while commits continue — still needs the harness its discriminator describes, and I did not want to assert what I had not measured. That closes the run. What it stands on: three execution-grounded findings with retained receipts, declared comparisons, witnesses and scoped limits — the startup replay that blocks NewRaft once the committed-but-unapplied window exceeds the FSM channel's batch capacity, shown with the default snapshot settings in force and with the constructor's blocked stack in the retained run; the nonvoter acknowledgement that satisfies VerifyLeader's voter quorum, sustained over twenty of twenty mixed-timer trials, coinciding with committed state the confirming leader never applied in twelve of twelve, and bounded for uniform clusters down to a one-millisecond margin with the gate that produces the separation identified; and the membership change that installs a voter immediately against two published descriptions that promise staging, stranding a single-voter cluster until the added server runs or an operator intervenes out of band — alongside four refuted suspicions and one excluded cause, each with the evidence that settled it, one behaviour entry corrected under its own id with its affected use answered, twelve registered questions answered, no necessary gap outstanding, and one paused lead now carrying both its anchors and the source-level bound that distinguishes it from the first finding.
